title: How to reference a cell on another sheet
task: The basics of pulling a value from another tab into a formula — and the one syntax that changes between apps.
keywords: pull value from other sheet google sheets

excel.note: SheetName!Cell. Just type = then click the cell on the other tab and Excel builds it.

google_sheets.note: Identical. To pull from a different FILE, wrap in IMPORTRANGE (Sheets-only).

libreoffice.note: LibreOffice uses a DOT (Summary.B2), not an exclamation mark.

explanation: Any formula can reach other tabs by prefixing the cell with the sheet name: Summary!B2 times Data!C5 gives 12 x 5 = 60. Excel and Google Sheets use SheetName!Cell; LibreOffice uses SheetName.Cell (a dot) — so a workbook saved from one and opened in the other translates the separator automatically, but hand-typed formulas need the right one. Sheet names with spaces go in single quotes: ='Q1 Data'!A1. Referencing a cell in a completely separate FILE needs external links (Excel/LibreOffice) or IMPORTRANGE (Google Sheets only).
